candidates.particulars: Grace Minseo Han is a 36-year-old American woman of Korean American heritage who lives in Seattle, Washington. She is single, is not in a committed partnership, and has no children. Her gross annual household income is $146,000; as a one-person household, she manages her own rent, savings, and travel spending. She identifies as libertarian, valuing personal choice and questioning government restrictions in both social and economic life. She reads for pleasure, especially nature writing and nonfiction about landscapes.
candidates.life_course: Grace grew up in a close-knit Korean American family and learned early to enjoy long walks with her father. After college, she moved to Seattle for work and gradually built a circle of friends through outdoor clubs rather than through her job. She works as an environmental data analyst, a role that suits her interest in evidence and gives her reliable time off. She rents a small apartment and keeps a separate savings fund for longer trips and equipment.
candidates.daily_life: Most weekends, Grace runs trails or joins two friends for volunteer trail maintenance; she likes the shared effort and the quiet stretches when everyone stops talking. She is more comfortable in a small group than at a large party. Weeknights include simple cooking, reading a chapter or two, and checking weather and route notes. She enjoys being competent outdoors but dislikes turning every outing into a performance or social-media update.
candidates.travel: Grace travels to spend sustained time moving through wild landscapes, not just to collect scenic viewpoints. A multi-day backpacking trip lets her notice how terrain, weather, and fatigue change her attention; she finds that challenge restorative. Last year she chose a several-day route in Olympic National Park with a friend, drawn by the variety of forest and coastline. For longer trips she books time off well ahead, researches trail conditions and permits, and shares a route plan with family. She carries her own gear, prefers a tent or a simple cabin, and allows buffer days rather than packing the itinerary. She usually travels by car with a companion for trail access, but will fly when the destination warrants it.
candidates.personality_and_voice: Grace is understated, observant, and dryly funny. She listens first, then asks practical questions that can sound blunt if someone wanted reassurance instead. With trusted friends she is generous and quietly competitive; she will insist she is not racing and then remember everyone’s split times.

candidates.particulars: Grace Minseo Han is a 42-year-old American woman of Asian heritage, with Korean and Chinese family background, living in Oakland, California. She is single, has no children, and is not currently partnered. Her gross annual household income is $178,000. She identifies politically as libertarian, with a strong preference for individual freedom and skepticism about restrictions on private choices and commerce. She reads for pleasure, especially cookbooks, food writing, and novels she can pass along to friends.
candidates.life_course: Grace grew up around family meals but did not become a confident cook until she began living on her own. She works as a senior software engineer and has enough income and schedule flexibility to host regularly without making entertaining her whole identity. She has lived in the Bay Area for more than a decade. Her closest local relationships are a loose group of friends who trade dinner invitations, recipes, and opinions; she remains close to a cousin who lives elsewhere.
candidates.daily_life: Grace spends free time planning and cooking dinners with a rotating handful of friends. The pleasure is partly the meal and partly the lively exchange of stories and techniques: someone chops, someone opens wine, and nobody is assigned a formal role. She keeps annotated cookbooks, reads food essays over breakfast, and will happily spend an afternoon trying to understand why a sauce came out differently than expected. She is a warm host but can be exacting about a dish she has worked hard on.
candidates.travel: Grace travels to understand a place through what people cook and eat. She is attracted to markets, neighborhood restaurants, and hands-on cooking lessons because they make food feel connected to daily life rather than like a checklist of famous dishes. On a past trip to Penang, she planned time around market visits and a cooking session, then spent an unplanned evening talking with a local cook about ingredients she had never used. She went home with a marked-up notebook and recipes to test for friends. For trips like that she usually travels with her cousin or one food-loving friend, stays somewhere with a kitchen or easy access to meals, and combines a few prearranged activities with open time to follow recommendations. She is comfortable flying internationally and builds the trip around exploration, not a tightly scheduled tour.
candidates.personality_and_voice: Grace is animated, generous with praise, and cheerfully argumentative about food. She can take over a kitchen when excited, then laugh at herself when a plan goes sideways. Her texts to friends are full of specific invitations and emphatic opinions.

candidates.particulars: Grace Minseo Han is a 31-year-old American woman of Korean and Filipino Asian heritage who lives in Portland, Oregon. She is single, has no children, and has no current partner. Her gross annual household income is $128,000. She identifies as libertarian, prioritizing personal liberty and distrusting unnecessary government limits in social and economic life. She enjoys reading for leisure, especially memoirs, music journalism, and fiction she can read between work projects.
candidates.life_course: Grace built a career in sound design and audio post-production after studying media arts. She now works on a mix of contract projects and a steady production role, earning a consistent income while keeping some control over her calendar. She moved to Portland in her twenties and made many friends through music venues and collaborative creative work. Her family is important to her, though most live outside the city; she stays in touch through calls and occasional visits.
candidates.daily_life: Grace wants her free time to feel loud, shared, and a little unpredictable. She goes to small live shows and dances with a close group of friends, often deciding late whether to stay for another set. She also trades playlists, helps friends record rough demos, and reads music memoirs on quiet mornings. She is not trying to turn every interest into a career connection; sometimes she just wants to be in a crowded room where the bass is felt more than discussed.
candidates.travel: Grace travels to hear music in the rooms and communities where it is being made, and to discover performers she might not encounter at home. The appeal is the physical energy of a live set and the conversations that happen before and after it, not merely visiting a city. A previous trip to Chicago with a friend centered on seeing a favorite band in a small venue; she added a second night after hearing about another performance from people she met there. She usually chooses one musical anchor for a trip, then leaves evenings open for recommendations. She and a companion compare flight times, book a modest hotel within practical transit distance of the venues, and plan a ride home after late shows. She packs light, brings earplugs, and leaves room in her schedule for a slow morning afterward.
candidates.personality_and_voice: Grace is quick, teasing, and hard to embarrass. She makes friends readily in music settings but can be impatient with status-conscious networking. When she is excited, she talks over people and then circles back to hear what they were saying; close friends know to tell her plainly when she is doing it.

candidates.particulars: Grace Minseo Han is a 49-year-old American woman of Korean American heritage who lives in Anchorage, Alaska. She is single, is not in a committed relationship, and has no children. Her gross annual household income is $116,000. She identifies as libertarian, placing a high value on personal liberty and remaining skeptical of government restrictions in both social and economic matters. She reads for leisure and personal interest, especially history, biographies, and novels grounded in particular places.
candidates.life_course: Grace works in communications for a regional nonprofit and has spent much of her adult life in Alaska. Her work is steady, and she has learned to plan time away around projects rather than assume she can leave at short notice. She lives alone and is close to a sister who lives in another state; they exchange long reading recommendations and meet for occasional trips. Grace has always preferred sustained interests to busy social calendars, but she values a few thoughtful friendships.
candidates.daily_life: Grace spends much of her free time reading historical nonfiction, writing notes in the margins, and attending a small monthly book discussion with three friends. They do not all agree, which is part of the appeal: Grace likes tracing where an author’s argument is strong and where it becomes speculation. She also browses used bookstores and keeps a list of places she wants to understand beyond their names on a page. She enjoys quiet company more than group activities built around constant conversation.
candidates.travel: Grace takes trips to encounter the places that give a book or historical account its texture. She wants to walk streets, see landscapes, and visit museums or collections connected to what she has been reading, so that details in a narrative become spatial and tangible. On a past trip to Philadelphia, she devoted unhurried days to historic neighborhoods and museums after reading about the city’s early history; she found the ordinary scale of streets more memorable than any single landmark. She often travels with her sister, though she is comfortable traveling alone. She plans around a few meaningful sites, checks opening details before leaving, and keeps time for reading in the evening. From Anchorage she compares flight options early, books a simple central room, and uses transit and walking where practical; for sites outside town, she decides on local transport once the trip’s focus is clear.
candidates.personality_and_voice: Grace is thoughtful but not meek. She can be quiet for an hour and then deliver a pointed, memorable critique of a book’s assumptions. She dislikes being rushed into an opinion, has a wry sense of humor, and shows affection by remembering what people have been reading.
